title: Meet the Press Makes Its Television Debut on NBC
summary: On November 6, 1947, Meet the Press, which had begun on radio two years earlier, aired its first television episode on NBC.

body.text: According to the Library of Congress, Meet the Press began on Mutual Radio on October 5, 1945, with Martha Rountree as moderator and Lawrence Spivak as producer. It reached television two years later: its first television episode aired on NBC on November 6, 1947, again with Rountree moderating. The format brought four newspaper reporters together to question a prominent figure in the news. NBC News lists Rountree as moderator from November 6, 1947, to November 1, 1953. The Library of Congress holds thousands of hours of the program on film and audio, from a 1986 NBC donation.

sources.title: Fast facts about the longest-running program in television history

title: The UN General Assembly Sets Up a Committee Against Apartheid
summary: On November 6, 1962, the United Nations General Assembly adopted resolution 1761, which created the Special Committee against Apartheid.

body.text: On November 6, 1962, the United Nations General Assembly adopted resolution 1761 (XVII). South African History Online records that the resolution established the Special Committee against Apartheid, with the task of keeping the racial policies of the South African government under review throughout the year. The committee began its work in April 1963. South African History Online lists its main aims as pressing for sanctions against the government in Pretoria, helping the victims of apartheid and the liberation movements, and publicizing the abuses of apartheid.
